record.paper_title: Open Questions on Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics of Chemical Reaction Networks
record.context_brief: Chemical fluctuations in realistic biochemical networks
record.original_question: How can methods for studying chemical fluctuations in nonlinear chemical reaction networks that display nonequilibrium phase transitions be extended beyond analytically tractable minimal models to realistic biochemical networks that perform biologically interesting tasks?

evidence.quote: Chemical fluctuations have been studied in nonlinear CRNs displaying nonequilibrium phase transitions, but mostly using minimal models chosen to push analytical calculation as far as possible. The methods used (which are already nontrivial) need to be extended to study realistic biochemical networks performing interesting tasks.

artifact.status_search_result: This is posed as an open research direction in the field of nonequilibrium thermodynamics of chemical reaction networks. While substantial progress has been made on minimal nonlinear CRNs (e.g., Schlögl model, toggle switches) using WKB and large-deviation methods, no general framework is established for high-dimensional realistic biochemical networks with phase transitions; the question remains an active open problem.
